text:
Configuration and administration
Last Updated
: 2026-10-23

Use the reference information in this section to accomplish the configuration and administration tasks that address your business needs.

IBM App Connect Enterprise commands
Policy properties
IBM App Connect Enterprise commands
All IBM App Connect Enterprise Toolkit and runtime commands that are provided on Windowsand Linux systems are listed, with references to command details.
TADataCollector command
If you are transforming your architecture to adopt containers, use the TADataCollector command to analyze data from backup files of your IBM Integration Bus 10.0, IBM App Connect Enterprise 11.0, or IBM App Connect Enterprise 12.0 integration node or deployable BAR file.
Policy properties
Control and update connection properties and other operational properties at run time by overriding message flow and message flow node properties with a policy.

Message flows
Use the reference information in this section to develop your message flows and related resources.
Built-in nodes
IBM App Connect Enterprise supplies built-in nodes that you can use to define your message flows.
Discovery connector request node actions and behavior
When you use a discovery connector request node in a message flow, the behavior of the flow depends on the actions that you set when you configured the node during discovery and on the availability of any objects that you want to retrieve or update.
LocalEnvironment structure for connector input and request nodes
When a message is propagated by a discovery connector input node or a discovery connector request node, the output local environment is updated with details from the interaction with the remote service or server.
Transformation interfaces
View the reference material associated with the different ways in which you can transform messages in message flows.
User-defined patterns (reference)
View the reference information in this section to modify user-defined patterns and to create user-defined editors for your user-defined patterns. To write code to modify pattern instances when a pattern instance is generated by a pattern user, use the IBM Integration API and the PHP API. To write code for user-defined editors, use the Java interfaces for user-defined editors.
Message model reference information
Reference information in this section can help you develop and configure message models.

text:
Resource managers and their properties
Last Updated

You can influence the behavior of IBM® App Connect Enterprise by editing the properties for resource managers.

Resource managers in IBM App Connect Enterprise

The following table lists the resource managers that are available in IBM App Connect Enterprise. You can view the resource managers by accessing the web user interface as described in Accessing the web user interface and selecting the Resource managers tab.

You can update resource managers by using the REST API. For more information, see Updating the HTTPS Connector resource manager by using the administration REST API.

title: Security requirements for administrative tasks
source: IBM Documentation — App Connect Enterprise 12.0.x Reference
text:
Security requirements for administrative tasks
Last Updated
: 2026-10-23

You can set permissions to control the actions that users can complete on an integration node and its resources. Specific security requirements for administrative tasks vary according to the platform that you are using.

This section contains the following topics:
Tasks and authorizations for administration security
Commands and authorizations for administration security
Security requirements for Linux and AIX systems
Security requirements for Windows systems
Tasks and authorizations for administration security
If you enable integration node administration security, users require specific permissions so that they can complete administration tasks.
Commands and authorizations for administration security
If you have enabled administration security, users require specific permissions to be able to run the administration commands.
Security requirements for Linux and AIX systems
View a summary of the authorizations in a Linux and AIX environment.
Security requirements for Windows systems
Security requirements depend on the administrative task that you want to run.
Parent topic:
Reference

title: Test Client
source: IBM Documentation — App Connect Enterprise 12.0.x Reference
text:
Test Client
Last Updated
: 2026-10-23

You can use the Test Client to test your message flows.

You can use the Test Client to send test messages to message flows that use any of the input nodes that are specified in the following topic: Test Client overview.

The following topics provide reference information to help you to use the Test Client effectively:

Test Client overview
Test Client Events tab
Enqueue
Dequeue
Test Client Configuration tab
Test Client preferences
Deployment Location wizard
JMS events in the Test Client
Test Client overview
Use the Test Client to test message flows in a safe environment before they are used in a production system.
Test Client Events tab
You can use the Events tab in the Test Client to edit the properties and content of your test messages. You also view test events in the Events tab when you run the test.
Test Client Configuration tab
Configure your test environment in the Configuration tab in the Test Client.
Test Client preferences
You can set test settings for the local test environment that are used by the IBM App Connect Enterprise Test Client.
Deployment Location wizard
Use the Deployment Location wizard to set the integration server to which the test message flow is deployed. You can also use the wizard to create an integration node, a connection to a remote integration node, and a new integration server.
JMS events in the Test Client
Use the information in this topic to help you to understand JMS events in the Test Client.
Parent topic:
Reference

title: Troubleshooting
source: IBM Documentation — App Connect Enterprise 12.0.x Reference
text:
Troubleshooting
Last Updated
: 2026-10-23

Use the reference information in this section to help you diagnose errors in IBM® App Connect Enterprise.

Select the appropriate topic from the following list to diagnose problems and errors in IBM App Connect Enterprise:

Logs
Using trace
Trace logging from a user-defined C extension
Dumps
Abend files
IBM MQ facilities
Database facilities
Solutions to similar problems
Logs
If an error is reported by an IBM App Connect Enterprise component, start your investigations into its causes by looking at the product and systems logs to which information is written during component operation.
Dumps
Under exceptional circumstances, Windows MiniDumps, or UNIX core dumps might be produced.
Abend files
When a process does not end normally an abend file is generated.
Abend in a user-defined extension
Information that applies only when you have written your own C language user-defined extension.
IBM MQ facilities
Some IBM App Connect Enterprise components are dependent on IBM MQ resources. You can therefore gain valuable information from the IBM MQ logs and events.
Database facilities
The database products used by IBM App Connect Enterprise also record information that might be useful if you have any problems with their access.
Solutions to similar problems
Various sources of information about problems with IBM licensed programs and their use.
Parent topic:
Reference
